title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §§1-4 of these notes). M* = ⊕_{0≤α≤2n} M^α is a graded cohomology-type object, a model for H*(X) of a smooth projective n-fold. F = End(M*) is the graded ring of all 'correspondences'. Σ ⊂ F is a graded subring containing 1, a model for algebraic correspondences modulo homological equivalence. π_i are the Künneth projectors onto M^i. They satisfy:
- (1.1): π_i π_j = δ_ij π_i and Σ π_i = 1;
- (1.3): compatibility with the grading;
- (3.0): π_i = 0 for i ∉ [0,2n].

Condition (1.4)_i asks for v_i ∈ Σ of degree 2n−2i and w_i ∈ Σ of degree −(2n−2i) such that:
- w_i v_i π_i = π_i and v_i w_i π_{2n−i} = π_{2n−i}, i.e. v_i restricted to M^i is an isomorphism onto M^{2n−i} with inverse induced by w_i;
- w_i π_{2n−i} = π_i w_i.
This is an abstract 'Lefschetz-type' (Hard Lefschetz with algebraic inverse) condition. The model case is v_i = L^{n−i} with w_i its algebraic inverse, i.e. standard conjecture B.

Claim (5.1): if (1.4)_i holds for all i, then all π_i lie in Σ. Abstractly, this is Lefschetz-type B implies Künneth C.

Proof by descending induction on the excluded middle range. Assume π_α ∈ Σ for α ∉ [i, 2n−i]; we want π_i, π_{2n−i} ∈ Σ.
- With the notation of §3, φ_i = Σ_{α≥i} π_α = 1 − Σ_{α<i} π_α and ψ_{2n−i} = Σ_{α≤2n−i} π_α both lie in Σ by the induction hypothesis.
- v'_i := ψ_{2n−i} v_i φ_i ∈ Σ. Since v_i raises degree by 2n−2i, the only surviving component starts in degree α = i, so v'_i = π_{2n−i} v_i π_i.
- Likewise w'_i := φ_i w_i ψ_{2n−i} = π_i w_i π_{2n−i} ∈ Σ.
- Then w'_i v'_i = π_i w_i π_{2n−i} v_i π_i = π_i π_i w_i v_i π_i = π_i, and v'_i w'_i = π_{2n−i}.
- Hence π_i and π_{2n−i} are products of elements of Σ, so they lie in Σ.
- The middle projector π_n = 1 − Σ_{α≠n} π_α is then in Σ automatically.

Purpose: an algebraic proof, inside the 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' formalism, that a Lefschetz-type standard conjecture forces the Künneth components of the diagonal to be algebraic. The next page sharpens this with the actual Lefschetz operator L ∈ Σ² (conditions 6.1–6.3) and the primitive decomposition.
errors: The hypothesis w_i π_{2n−i} = π_i w_i is automatic once w_i is homogeneous of degree −(2n−2i) in a graded ring. Grothendieck uses it as if extra, but this is harmless.
The final reduction 'w_i v_i π_i = π_i' turns π_i π_i (w_i v_i π_i) into π_i·π_i·π_i = π_i. The marginal 'π_i^3 = π_i' is correct, just compressed.

The base/trivial case is stated as 'i = n−1, suppose i ≤ n−2' (as read). Logically the trivial case is the last step, π_n = 1 − Σ_{α≠n} π_α, i.e. i = n. For i = n−1 one still needs the argument. This is either a misreading or an off-by-one slip in indexing; no mathematical gap.
Implicit assumption: 1 ∈ Σ, needed for φ_i and ψ_{2n−i} to lie in Σ. This is presumably part of 'sous-anneau'.

ideas.what: If for each i ≤ n there is an algebraic correspondence of degree 2n−2i inducing an isomorphism H^i → H^{2n−i} whose inverse is also algebraic, then all Künneth projectors are algebraic.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B (or its weak 'algebraic isomorphism' form) implies Künneth standard conjecture C
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (stated in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles', Bombay 1968/69); proof written by Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay Colloquium 1968, publ. 1969), statement that B implies C

ideas.what: Truncation trick: use partial sums of known projectors (φ_i, ψ_{2n−i}) to cut a homogeneous correspondence down to its single component M^i → M^{2n−i}, then invert inside Σ.
ideas.modern_name: Descending induction on Künneth components via degree truncation (as in Kleiman's proof of B ⇒ C)

ideas.what: Abstract framework: a graded subring Σ of End(M*) inside a graded ring F, with Künneth-type idempotents. This is a purely algebraic 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' formalism for the standard conjectures.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/abstract treatment of standard conjectures (graded endomorphism algebras, Weil cohomology formalism)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (1968, 1994); André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004) for later axiomatic treatments

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct proof that a Lefschetz-type condition implies algebraicity of the Künneth projectors, i.e. B ⇒ C. Grothendieck stated this and Kleiman published essentially the same argument in 1968. The abstract graded-ring packaging and the use of an arbitrary algebraic isomorphism with algebraic inverse (not necessarily L^{n−i}) are mildly interesting archival details. They are not new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '[-Pour supposons prouvé par fait-]' is better read as a struck-out 'Pour ce, supposons prouvé (5.1) pour i …', followed by the inserted 'i.e. π_α ∈ Σ si α ∉ [i, 2n−i]'.
'l'on veut remplacer i par i+1' is in context 'et l'on veut remplacer i par i+1, i.e. prouver que π_i et π_{2n−i} ∈ Σ'.
Line '(car w_i π_{2n−i} = π_i w_i)' is the first marginal justification. The second marginal note reads '(car w_i v_i π_i = π_i)' above '= π_i^3 = π_i'.
In '[p.ex. l'anneau des correspondances d'un M* comme dans 1.]', the word 'l'anneau' is an insertion above a struck word.

'Notons que, avec les notations de 3.' is followed by a struck fragment ('v_i, w_i …'), with 'dans' inserted above. The intended sentence is 'les éléments ψ_{2n−i} v_i φ_i, φ_i w_i ψ_{2n−i} ∈ Σ; ici …'.
